focus_area: Independent second pass: sanitizeTrackingParams (SPEC 5.1/D4), the 5-preamble wire contract (allKeysToSnake), the utmData inner-key contract (D2, 7.9), and GoogleSSOButton hidden-input encoding (5.3/D7)

findings.title: Surrogate-safe truncation in sanitizeTrackingValue is shipped, sanctioned behavior that SPEC.md 5.1 rule 2 / 7.1 never absorbed - spec amendment needed, not a code change
findings.spec_requirement: SPEC.md 5.1 rule 2: 'Truncate string values to 255 characters.' and 7.1: '255-char truncation per value'. Neither mentions the surrogate-boundary behavior.
findings.evidence: app/javascript/shared/lib/utils.js lines 35-39 at fc3f047f9: after slice(0, 255), a trailing lone high surrogate (charCode 0xd800-0xdbff) is dropped, yielding a 254-code-unit value at that boundary. Introduced by commit fa51c91a5 ('Make tracking param truncation surrogate-safe in sanitizeTrackingParams'), the sanctioned fix for qa-run-2 Layer 2 finding l2-B1 (HIGH, orchestrator-reproduced: naive slice could split a surrogate pair, ES2019 JSON.stringify emits a lone \udXXX escape, Rails json 2.6.1 rejects the body and the signup POST 400s - see reviews/QA-COMPLETE.md). Empirically re-verified in this round: a 254-char + emoji input truncates to 254 units and JSON round-trips cleanly. The code is correct and the fix is settled; the finding is that the spec text was never amended. A future implementer or reviewer working from SPEC.md as the authority would write a bare slice(0,255) and reintroduce the qa-run-2 HIGH, and the current code is a literal mismatch with the spec sentence ('255 characters' vs 254 code units at the boundary). Not a re-report of l2-B1 itself and not among the settled M1-M4/9-LOW rulings in QA-MED-FINDINGS.md.
findings.recommendation: Amend SPEC.md 5.1 rule 2 (and the 7.1 restatement) to record the sanctioned behavior, e.g.: 'Truncate string values to 255 UTF-16 code units; if the slice ends in a lone high surrogate, drop it (254 units) so the value JSON-serializes cleanly (qa-run-2 l2-B1 fix, commit fa51c91a5).' No code change.

5.1 library fact 2 re-verified: default arrayFormat 'none' formatter (index.js lines 79-87) builds repeated-param arrays via [].concat in occurrence order; final reduce's !Array.isArray(value) guard (line 159) passes arrays through the sort untouched; confirmed by execution (['first','second']). So value[0] in sanitizeTrackingValue (utils.js:32) is the first occurrence - rule 1 holds

5.1 key-derivation parity: helper's occurrence scan (utils.js:51-52, param.replace(/\+/g,' ').split('=')[0] then decodeUriComponent) matches parse's own key handling (index.js:148 identical replace/split, line 99-105 decode via the same decode-uri-component package) - fix 299cf9465 verified live (encoded utm%5Fmedium counted and captured)

5.1 rules 1-3 + absence semantics verified by execution against a verbatim transliteration of the HEAD helper: first-of-repeated; 255 truncation (300->255, 255->255); 12 distinct non-alphabetical utm_* keys -> first 10 by raw-string occurrence order (alphabetical-parse implementation would fail this input); '' -> {}; '?foo=bar' -> {}; no utmData key fabrication; absent fields absent; '?utm_source' -> null; '?utm_source=' -> ''; utm_source/utm_campaign excluded from utmData, internal_ref never in utmData

5-preamble wire contract: apiPost is app/javascript/shared/queryHooks/api.ts:25 -> apiMutate line 52 data: skipKeysToSnake ? variables : allKeysToSnake(variables); register (useSession.ts:39) and magicLink (useSession.ts:91) call apiPost WITHOUT skipKeysToSnake so the transform runs (contrast: login passes skipKeysToSnake: true); allKeysToSnake imported from @ats/src/lib/utils/structure (api.ts:2) matching the spec's stated path app/javascript/ats/src/lib/utils/structure.js

allKeysToSnake recursion confirmed: structure.js:94-124, line 104 newObject[snakeCase(key)] = allKeysToSnake(object[key], modifyValues) - recurses into nested plain objects, so utmData inner keys are snakeCased in transit; snakeCase facts confirmed by execution: utmSource->utm_source, utmCampaign->utm_campaign, utmData->utm_data, internalRef->internal_ref; utm_medium/utm_term/utm_content/utm_id/utm_source_platform unchanged; utm_content2->utm_content_2 (spec's stated fact, 5-preamble and Risk 3)

wire-to-permit match: the four transformed names utm_source/utm_campaign/utm_data/internal_ref are exactly what sign_up_params permits (registrations_controller.rb:310 at HEAD: ..., :utm_source, :utm_campaign, :internal_ref, utm_data: {} - hash-permit trailing per 4.1); magic_create reads sign_up_params[:utm_source|:utm_campaign|:utm_data|:internal_ref] in both branches; absent camelCase fields are undefined, JSON.stringify drops them, wire param never arrives, column stays nil (absence chain confirmed)

D2/7.9 inner-key contract: helper stores inner keys as the decoded raw URL param names (utils.js:82, key from the occurrence scan - no camelCasing); JSON-path in-transit normalization is the spec-stated existing mechanism; SSO form path posts keys verbatim (Risk 3 wording matches code)

5.3 GoogleSSOButton.tsx at HEAD (lines 9-18 Props; 20-29 destructuring; 58-80 inputs): Props extended with utmSource?/utmCampaign?/utmData?: Record<string,any>/internalRef?; three string inputs guarded by the exact analog pattern typeof x === 'string' && x.length > 0 (analog referral line 59-61, partner 62-64; new 65-73); input names are snake_case literals utm_source/utm_campaign/internal_ref; utm_data rendered one hidden input per key with name={'utm_data[' + key + ']'} (line 77), outer guard utmData != undefined (house null/undefined form) + identical per-key guard typeof utmData[key] === 'string' && utmData[key].length > 0 - so null (valueless) and '' (empty) render no input, the spec's stated consequence; inputs live inside the existing form action='/api/v1/users/auth/google_oauth2' method='post' submitted via formElement.submit() (native POST, no axios, allKeysToSnake bypassed - snake_case literals required and present)
diff-to-spec direction for GoogleSSOButton.tsx: every changed hunk line traces to 5.3 (Props extension, destructuring, four input blocks); no other change in the file

notes: Repo verified at fc3f047f9 on attribution-work-qa before review. Empirical work: query-string order facts and lodash snakeCase confirmed by executing against the repo's own node_modules; helper behavior confirmed by running a verbatim CJS transliteration of the HEAD code (scratchpad only, repo untouched) - all 20 assertions pass, including a 12-key non-alphabetical cap input that an alphabetical-order implementation would fail (per pipeline rule 28). Settled items observed and NOT re-flagged: sanitizer throw on non-string input and '?'-less utmData drop (LOW 4), key length uncapped (LOW 3), decode-uri-component phantom dependency (LOW 5), bracket-key SSO 400 (M3), SSO session ride untyped/uncapped (M1). The single finding is a spec-text amendment item for already-sanctioned code (fa51c91a5), filed because Layer 1's authority document still reads 'truncate to 255 characters' with no record of the surrogate-boundary behavior. One conforming nuance worth recording: parse() creates a ''-key entry for empty params ('a=1&&b=2') which the helper's occurrence scan skips (utils.js:50) - no divergence possible for tracking fields since '' never starts with utm_ and is not a named param. Also confirmed utm_data as a literal URL param name (?utm_data=y) lands inside utmData as inner key 'utm_data' per the 'every other utm_* param' contract - conforming, wire name utm_data[utm_data].
